note: M16.18's device/browser matrix: the platforms the client is certified on, the text surfaces each one exercises, and the reason for anything it does not. Each covered profile is a real engine at a real screen, driven by TestM1618PlatformMatrix through engine/web/test/platform_matrix.test.mjs. This file is a claim, not a run log — the test fails if a profile covered less (or more) than it declares, and the parity report (cmd/zzt-parity) refuses to certify while a skipped profile carries no reason. Touch GAMEPLAY is certified by the profiles that set `touchplay` (M16.18a, landed 2026-08-01): those runs play the CONTROL world with no keyboard at all — the pad walks, Fire shoots both of vanilla's ways, a torch is carried to the dark board and lit, and the game is paused and un-paused — with every act tick-locked on the input frame the server received. Only the Chromium touch profiles declare it, because they are the only ones where the on-screen bar exists (see webkit-touch-portrait). Reading the screenshots in engine/web/test-results: a tall phone page is captured in slices and a `position: fixed` control bar can be drawn once per slice, so the bar may appear at the top of a portrait screenshot as well as at the bottom. Where it really is comes from the measured rects, which the suite asserts are entirely in the bottom half of the viewport. The inventory gained a seventh surface on 2026-08-03 (M19.2’s color picker); every covered profile explains it rather than exercising it, and M16.18d is the filed task that brings it into the battery.

profiles.label: Chromium touch emulation, portrait 390x844 @3x

surfacesOmitted.colorPicker: exercised on a Chromium touch profile by TestM192ColorPickerJourney (M19.2), which opens the window by tapping the on-screen bar’s Color button and picks a color with the pad and Enter alone. Not run through this profile’s battery because the battery types a fixed seed plus "X" and then s/t/b/q, which assumes a field that accepts any character; the picker’s is filtered to hex digits, so certifying it here means parameterising the battery — filed as M16.18d.

profiles.notes: The 80-column screen is 4.88 CSS px per column here, and the whole grid including the sidebar is on it — the width binds in portrait, so reserving the control bar's height (M16.18b) moved the screen up without shrinking it. Rotated to landscape it used to be the other way round: the letterboxed canvas filled the viewport's height and the fixed bar lay on the bottom seven text rows. Both lists are zero as of M16.18b (2026-08-01), which is the fix's evidence: the bar publishes its measured height and the screen letterboxes above it. This is also one of the two profiles that certify touch GAMEPLAY (M16.18a): the bar's five play-mode controls wrap to two rows at this width, and the reservation is measured rather than assumed for exactly that reason.

profiles.label: Chromium touch emulation, landscape 844x390 @3x

Not run through this profile’s battery because the battery types a fixed seed plus "X" and then s/t/b/q, which assumes a field that accepts any character; the picker’s is filtered to hex digits, so certifying it here means parameterising the battery — filed as M16.18d.

profiles.notes: The shape that found M16.18b: the height binds here, so before the fix the letterboxed canvas filled all 390px of it and the fixed control bar covered rows 18-24 — the bottom of the board and the sidebar's Save/Pause/Quit block. Zero as of M16.18b (2026-08-01): the bar reserves its height (112px at this width, the direction pad's two rows, with the five play-mode controls on one action row) and the screen letterboxes into the 278px above it at 6.35 CSS px per column, which is still well over the legibility floor. Text entry was unaffected throughout — every surface passed before the fix as well.

profiles.notes: Playwright's WebKit delivers touch events but reports navigator.maxTouchPoints 0, so this profile certifies the client's OTHER touch gate: MobileTextInputBridge's `touchSeen` fallback, which mounts the native control on the first touch the canvas sees. That is the path a hybrid device with an unreliable maxTouchPoints takes. Real iOS Safari reports 5 and would take the maxTouchPoints path Chromium takes above; the on-screen control bar, decided once at load, is correctly absent here — which is also why this profile does not declare `touchplay`: there are no controls here to play with, and the gameplay path it WOULD take on a real iPhone is the one the two Chromium touch profiles certify.

profiles.label: Firefox touch emulation, portrait 390x844 @3x
profiles.reason: Playwright cannot emulate touch in Firefox: with hasTouch set the context still reports navigator.maxTouchPoints 0 and exposes no touch events, so a run here would certify a synthetic path no Firefox build produces. Firefox is covered desktop-only above, and both touch gates a Firefox-on-a-touchscreen build could take are certified on the Chromium and WebKit touch profiles.
